title: Split Panes
narrative:
In this specification you can not only see how to use the Swing-Tree API to
   create and configure split panes but also how to bind them to your view model model.
   The axis a split pane is laid out along, for example, can be bound to a property in your view model.

features.id: A split pane laid out along the horizontal axis can be created through the "splitPane" factory method.

blocks.text: We create a split pane UI node laid out along the horizontal axis.
We actually build the component:
The split pane is a JSplitPane.
The split pane places its two components left and right of each other.

features.id: A split pane laid out along the vertical axis can be created through the "splitPane" factory method.

blocks.text: We create a split pane UI node laid out along the vertical axis.
We actually build the component:
The split pane is a JSplitPane.
The split pane places its two components above one another.

features.id: An `UI.Axis` property can be used to dynamically model the layout of your split pane.

extraInfo:
Note that the property shown in this example would be part of your view model.
            So you can simply modify it as part of your business logic and the split pane
            will automatically update the axis it is laid out along.

blocks.text: We create a simple view model property holding the axis of our split pane.
We create a split pane UI node bound to the property.
We actually build the component:
The split pane is a JSplitPane.
The split pane is laid out along the horizontal axis, meaning components are placed left to right.
We change the axis property to "VERTICAL".
The split pane is laid out along the vertical axis, meaning components are placed top to bottom.

features.id: An `UI.Axis` property can be used to dynamically model the layout of your split pane using `withLayoutOrientation(..)`.

extraInfo:
Note that the property shown in this example would be part of your view model.
            So you can simply modify it as part of your business logic and the split pane
            will automatically update the axis it is laid out along.

We change the axis property to "VERTICAL".
The split pane is laid out along the vertical axis, meaning components are placed top to bottom.

features.id: The divider location of a split pane can dynamically be modelled using an integer property.

extraInfo:
Note that the property shown in this example would be part of your view model.
            So you can simply modify it as part of your business logic and the split pane
            will automatically update its divider location based on an observer
            registered on the property.

We change the divider location property to 20.
The divider location is 20.
